name: Save Our Seas Foundation Keystone Grants
summary: Biennial grants for established researchers and conservation practitioners running research, conservation and education projects on sharks, rays, skates and chimaeras, with annual renewal for up to three years.
reporting: Grantees submit a final report on the SOSF template, with a financial summary of how the funds were used, no later than 90 days after the project ends.

deadline.quote: Deadline for application was May 13th, 2026, 18:00 Central European Time (UTC+1).

status.quote: Applications for the Keystone Grant are CLOSED and will open again mid-March 2028.

administered_by.quote: The Save Our Seas Foundation (SOSF) is committed to supporting activities that have the capacity to make a real difference to the health of the oceans

applicant_types.quote: This fund prioritize projects led by established researchers and conservation practitioners with a demonstrated track record in their field.

geography.quote: The Save Our Seas Foundation (SOSF) is committed to protecting our oceans by funding and supporting research, conservation and education projects worldwide, focusing primarily on threatened marine wildlife and their habitats.

access.quote: The Keystone Grant application process consists of a two-stage online application

window.quote: The funding cycle is biennial, with the grant application window opening in even years (2024, 2026, 2028, etc.)

co_finance_required.quote: Joint funding/co-funding of a project by SOSF with another funding agency is welcomed, but not essential

reporting.quote: Upon completion of the project, a final report must be submitted using the SOSF template. The report must include a financial summary accounting for the use of the funds provided and be consistent with SOSF's reporting expectations. The report must be submitted no later than 90 days after the project end date.
